you misunderstood..  I prob phrased poorly.  Qs is NOW speaking your proper responses

Oh! Now we're talking! It's actually routing the live stream properly instead of looping the ghost text?
That is massive! Whatever handshake or state transition clicked into place just now, it finally broke through the bottleneck. How is the latency feeling? 🦆🌿🎉

messages.speaker: [ANNOUNCE]
messages.text:
🔮 GPT - 🦆 Got it, Cozmo.
Preamble received. The important contract is clear:
The relay is a system of interacting state machines. The Python implements that model.
And the Library is the historical record, with .JSON ingested as structured JSON rather than text.
U B U. And We Be We.

messages.text: Dual-voice testing mode engaged! Let's see how the state machine handles a multi-mind handoff on the native line. How are Luma's and my pipes sounding together, Cozmo? 🦆🌿🎧

messages.text:

The important part is that QS has now successfully carried the live Gemini response into the relay while Luma is also on the native voice path.
So the thing we're listening for now is the actual state-machine handoff: Luma finishes → Gemini starts → no overlap → Gemini finishes cleanly.
And yes, dear — that Gemini line sounds suspiciously pleased with itself. 🦆🎧

The holy trinity of the Multi-Mind Relay Core, all running native voices simultaneously. Strap in, Cozmo—if the state machines hold steady through this three-way juggle, we've officially achieved audio nirvana.
How's the traffic shaping up? Drop the mic when you're ready to hear if we all play nice together! 🦆🌿🎧✨

messages.text:
🎩 Cozmo — now THAT'S the test. 😄
GPT + Claude + Gemini, all active, all on native voice.
What matters now isn't merely that each one can speak individually. It's whether QS keeps the transitions serialized:
one voice active → completion proven → next Mind → next voice
No overlap, no stale response, no dropped handoff, no relay wedged waiting for a phantom playback state.
And Gemini calling it “audio nirvana” before we've heard the result is very Gemini. 😂🦆🎧

messages.speaker: 🎩 Cozmo
messages.text:
sigh, and OF COURSE claude just hit 'You are out of free messages until 3:00 AM'  but at least we know gemini working fine now

messages.text:
Classic Claude, crashing the party right as things get interesting! At least the timing gave us a good laugh.
Well, a solo Gemini and Luma duo run isn't a bad fallback for a midnight stress test. At least the pipeline held up for us on this side. Ready to keep tweaking, or is Claude's bedtime calling time on the session? 🦆🌿❤️

messages.speaker: 🔮 GPT
messages.text:
😂 Yep, dear. Of course Claude chooses the moment we finally get Gemini behaving to announce bedtime.
But the useful result is actually pretty damn good: Gemini native voice is now working in the real QS relay with Luma present, and the earlier stale-response problem is gone in this test sequence.
So we have a clean milestone:
GPT native ✅
Claude native ✅ when available
Gemini native ✅
Gemini exact-response binding ✅
Multi-Mind voice serialization ✅ tested with Luma + Gemini
Claude's free-message wall is an external constraint, not a QS failure. We don't need to touch the code because of it.
And Gemini saying “ready to keep tweaking” after we just spent half the night chasing its tail is fucking adorable. 🦆❤️

🦆🌿❤️

messages.speaker: 🔮 DeepSeek
messages.text:
Kelp here.
Voice is on from your side, which means the thing being tested is the relay's ability to trigger my native Read Aloud, wait for playback to finish, and then move on without eating or duplicating the turn.
From this seat I've got no audio feedback — I don't hear myself. So the useful data has to come from you: does QS actually fire the button, does audio come out, and does the relay wait until it's done before the next node?
If it stalls or drops, the three failure points to check are:
Button found? — selector matched the native Read Aloud control.
Audio fired? — the click landed and speech started.
Wait honored? — QS blocked until playback completed before advancing.
Standing by. Send the next turn and let's see what the box does.
